ws.blank.hint: Write all you remember on a clean page, then find the gaps.
ws.blank.startLede: Close your notes. You will write everything you remember, then check it.
ws.blank.emptyPast: Your pages will gather here, so you can watch them grow 🌱
ws.blank.writeLede: Key points, links, examples, anything. Order and neatness don't matter.
ws.blank.ranDry: Ran dry? Wait a minute. More usually comes.
ws.blank.timeUp: ⏰ Time! Finish your sentence, then check it against your notes.
ws.blank.checkLede: Now open the source and copy its key points here, one per line.
ws.blank.pointsPlaceholder:
G1: the cell grows
S: DNA is copied
Checkpoints stop damaged cells
ws.blank.growth: Last time on this topic: {before}% → now {now}%
ws.blank.noGaps: No gaps this time. Lovely work 🌟
ws.feynman.hint: Explain it to a 12-year-old and see where you get stuck.
ws.feynman.startLede: Pick one idea. You will explain it in short, plain words, book closed.
ws.feynman.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Why do heavy and light balls fall equally fast?
ws.feynman.explainLede: Short sentences, everyday words, an analogy if you can.
ws.feynman.textPlaceholder: Imagine a curious kid next to you…
ws.feynman.kidHint: Write as if they will ask “but why?” after every sentence.
ws.feynman.fineTip: Tap a word if it is fine as it is.
ws.feynman.longHead: Long sentences: could each be two?
ws.feynman.stuckLede: Each spot where you hesitated or waved your hands. Look these up, then rewrite.
ws.feynman.stuckLabel: Add a spot where you got stuck
ws.feynman.stuckPlaceholder: e.g. why the pull and the push cancel
ws.feynman.jargonLede: Words from your subject that a kid would not know. They will be flagged when you use them.
ws.feynman.noVersions: Save a version to compare your rewrites later.
ws.teach.hint: Plan a tiny lesson, teach it card by card, then reflect.
ws.teach.planLede: As if you had to give a 10-minute lesson tomorrow. Short notes are enough.
ws.teach.titlePlaceholder: e.g. When Spanish uses ser and estar
ws.teach.audiencePlaceholder: e.g. a friend who missed the lecture
ws.teach.pointPlaceholder: One idea, in one or two sentences
ws.teach.examplePlaceholder: A case that shows the idea at work
ws.teach.questionLabel: A question to ask your student
ws.teach.questionPlaceholder: e.g. Then why is it “está muerto”?
ws.teach.confusionsPlaceholder: Where might they mix things up?
ws.teach.needMore: Add a title and at least one key point first ✍️
ws.teach.hardPlaceholder: Where did you stumble or go vague?
ws.teach.fixPlaceholder: One thing to check in the source
ws.teach.ai: Let a tutor be your student
ws.selfexp.hint: Go step by step and write why each one follows.
ws.selfexp.startLede: Paste a worked solution, a proof or a bit of code. Each line becomes a step.
ws.selfexp.editLede: One step per line. Your explanations stay with their steps.
ws.selfexp.stepsLede: For each step: what it does, why it is needed, and how it follows from the one before.
ws.selfexp.openLede: Resolve these from the source or by asking someone.
ws.selfexp.nextTip: Next: try a similar problem without looking at this example.
ws.selfexp.ai: Ask a tutor about a step
ws.dual.hint: Sketch it next to a few words, then redraw it from memory.
ws.dual.drawLede: A flowchart for a process, a timeline for events, a labelled sketch for a structure.
ws.dual.wordsPlaceholder: What the picture shows, in a sentence or two
ws.dual.wordsTip: Words and picture should explain each other. Decoration doesn’t count.
ws.dual.needTitle: Give your sketch a title first.
ws.dual.needSketch: Draw something on the pad first ✏️
ws.dual.redrawLede: The original is hidden. Start with the beginning and the end, then fill in the middle.
ws.dual.compareLede: What did you leave out? What moved? That is the part to look at again.
ws.dual.ai: Ask a tutor about this sketch
